stem:
A 30-year-old man becomes dehydrated during a desert trek, and his kidneys produce a small volume of highly concentrated urine. The ability to concentrate urine depends on a hyperosmolar renal medulla.

Which of the following properties of the loop of Henle most directly builds this medullary gradient?

options.label: A
options.text: The ascending limb extrudes sodium while remaining impermeable to water
options.misconception: None; solute pumping without water following is what raises interstitial osmolarity.
options.explanation: The ascending limb is completely impermeable to water (no aquaporins) yet actively pumps Na+ into the interstitium; the movement of Na+ and urea into the interstitial spaces creates the hyperosmotic environment of the medulla.

options.label: B
options.text: The vasa recta rapidly wash solutes out of the medullary interstitium
options.misconception: The gradient-preserving vessel is being described as gradient-destroying.
options.explanation: Slow flow in the vasa recta preserves the osmolar gradient while recovering solutes and water; rapid washout would dissipate the medullary hyperosmolarity.

options.label: C
options.text: The collecting duct pumps sodium against its gradient under ADH control
options.misconception: The site of medullary solute deposition is being misassigned.
options.explanation: ADH regulates water channels, not the salt pumping that builds the gradient; the multiplier is generated by the ascending limb (with urea from the collecting duct).

options.label: D
options.text: The descending limb is impermeable to water, trapping solute in the lumen
options.misconception: The water permeabilities of the two limbs are being reversed.
options.explanation: The descending limb is freely water-permeable via permanent aquaporins; it is the ascending limb that is impermeable to water while extruding Na+.

options.label: E
options.text: The descending limb actively pumps sodium into the medullary interstitium
options.misconception: The descending segment's role is being given the ascending limb's transporter.
options.explanation: The descending limb is water-permeable through permanent aquaporins and loses water to the interstitium; active Na+ extrusion is the work of the ascending limb.

context: Learning objective: explain the countercurrent multiplier. The water-impermeable ascending limb pumps Na+ into the interstitium; Na+ and urea accumulation creates medullary hyperosmolarity, enabling water recovery.
imageCaption: Countercurrent multiplier, inulin=GFR, fluid compartments, EPO, micturition.
